title: Jailer 2 Advance Bookings Near Rs 40 Crore Worldwide Ahead of October 15 Release
excerpt: Rajinikanth's sequel crossed Rs 37 crore in opening-day pre-sales by Monday evening with several shows yet to open, according to box-office trackers — three days before release.
body:
• Jailer 2's worldwide opening-day advance bookings approached Rs 40 crore by Monday, with trackers reporting more than Rs 37 crore in real-time pre-sales.
  • Several shows had yet to open for booking, leaving room for the figure to climb before the October 15 release.
  • The Nelson Dilipkumar-directed sequel brings Rajinikanth back as Muthuvel Pandian, with an ensemble including Vidya Balan, Mithun Chakraborty and S. J. Suryah, plus cameos by Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar, Jackie Shroff, Vijay Sethupathi and Hrithik Roshan.
  • Advance sales are not the final opening-day collection — occupancy from Thursday's screenings will decide the actual number.

Pre-sales build three days out

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 is approaching Rs 40 crore in worldwide advance bookings for its opening day, three days before the film reaches theatres. Box-office tracker Jerin Georgekutty reported on Monday evening that real-time advance sales had crossed Rs 37 crore, with several shows yet to open for bookings — meaning the pre-release figure still has headroom before Thursday.

https://x.com/sunpictures/status/2109275948424286474

"Pre-sales build three days out Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 is approaching Rs 40 crore in worldwide advance bookings for its opening day, three days before the film reaches theatres."

Advance booking numbers measure tickets sold before release, not the film's final opening-day gross; walk-in sales and opening-day occupancy will determine where the day-one total lands. Even so, a pre-sales tally of this size puts the sequel in rare company for a Tamil film and reflects the scale of the franchise after the first Jailer's blockbuster run in 2023.

The film

Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Kalanithi Maran's Sun Pictures, Jailer 2 is a Tamil action comedy in which Rajinikanth returns as retired jailer Muthuvel Pandian. Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu, Mirnaa and Rithvik return from the first film, joined by S. J. Suryah, Mithun Chakraborty, Suraj Venjaramoodu, Vidya Balan, Anna Rajan and Jatin Sarna. Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar, Jackie Shroff, Vijay Sethupathi and Hrithik Roshan appear in cameos. Anirudh Ravichander composes the music, with cinematography by Vijay Kartik Kannan.

For diaspora viewers

The film releases worldwide on Thursday, October 15, including in North America and the Gulf, where Rajinikanth's films traditionally open with early-morning fan shows. One wrinkle for Hindi-belt viewers: the Hindi version's multiplex rollout has been the subject of an OTT-window dispute this week — read our explainer, Jailer 2's Hindi Version Caught in Multiplex Row Over Four-Week OTT Window. In the US, expect the Tamil version with English subtitles to anchor most screens, with the Hindi and Telugu versions in major metros. The full advance-booking breakdown is at Filmibeat.

Reading the number

Pre-sales trackers caution — and Filmibeat's report notes — that advance figures are a snapshot of tickets sold, not a prediction. What they do measure reliably is intensity of demand in the film's strongest markets, and for Jailer 2 the pattern is familiar from the first film: heavy early buying in Tamil Nadu, strong Gulf and US pre-sales, and fan-driven first-day-first-show bookings that front-load the opening. The open question for the opening-day total is breadth — how much of the Hindi belt the film reaches on day one, given the multiplex dispute over its streaming window, and how much walk-in traffic the reviews generate on Thursday evening and Friday.

The sequel also arrives with unusual cross-industry casting for a Tamil film — Bollywood names in both the main cast and the cameo list — which the makers are counting on to widen the audience beyond Rajinikanth's core base. The first real test comes Wednesday night, when final pre-sale figures land, and Thursday morning, when occupancy reports from the earliest shows replace tracker estimates with counted tickets.
